clue.text: Complained of exercise in this square?

indicators.note: the exercise is placed in the middle of the square, so its letters go inside the other piece

parts.note: the crossword itself is laid out on a grid, the square the solver is looking at
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Someone moans about the fitness session held in this town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this square' is self-referential: the grid you are filling in.
explanation.definitionFit: To gripe is an informal synonym for grumbling, so griped means moaned or grumbled.

clue.text: Chairs about entrance to cabins on ships

indicators.note: in a down answer the cabin letter sits on top of the ships

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is its first letter

parts.note: liners are passenger ships

explanation.surface: Deckchairs are found near the entrance to cabins aboard ocean ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Recliners are armchairs whose backs tip back for lounging.

clue.text: It may have wings, but absolutely not power to rise

indicators.note: in a down answer rising means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: no sir is an emphatic refusal
P is the symbol for power in physics

explanation.surface: Something with wings that absolutely lacks the power to get airborne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' is a link word; wings here are prison blocks, not a bird's.
explanation.definitionFit: Prisons are built in wings, separate blocks off a central hall, so a jail may have wings.

clue.text: Observed screen did go haywire

indicators.note: going haywire means running out of control, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone saw the screen malfunction.
explanation.definitionFit: To discern is to perceive or notice, so discerned means seen or observed.

clue.text: Thought fun is late starting

indicators.note: something late in starting misses its opening, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: something amusing is fun

explanation.surface: Someone reflects that a good time has been slow to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word joining wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Musing is pondering or reflection, so as a noun it is a thought.

clue.text: Red Dwarf is beneath me

indicators.note: in a down answer the dwarf comes below the other piece

parts.note: Doc is one of the seven dwarfs in Snow White

explanation.surface: Someone says the TV show Red Dwarf is beneath them.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Dwarf is a British sitcom; here 'Red' is the definition, a wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Médoc is a Bordeaux wine region known for its red wines, so a Médoc is a red.

clue.text: Philosopher's very cheap cars

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
a crate is slang for an old, cheap car

explanation.surface: A philosopher drives very cheap cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Socrates was the Athenian thinker, the classic Greek philosopher.

clue.text: New measure of computer storage filling two clouds

indicators.note: the storage unit fills the space between the two letters

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals
MB is a megabyte

explanation.surface: A new unit of computer storage fills two clouds, cloud storage being the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimbi is the plural of nimbus, a rain cloud.

clue.text: Criticises financial centre; forgets what to say about it

indicators.note: the forgetful actor's word is placed around the other piece, surrounding it

parts.note: an actor who dries forgets their lines on stage
EC is the postcode of the City of London, Britain's financial centre

explanation.surface: A spokesperson attacks the City but is lost for words when asked about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The City of London's postcode stands for the financial centre; 'dries' is theatre slang for an actor forgetting lines.
explanation.definitionFit: To decry something is to denounce it publicly, which is to criticise it.

clue.text: Skilled with scalping, hotel make one pay a bomb

indicators.note: scalping removes the top, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: adept means skilled
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to charge is to make someone pay

explanation.surface: Skilled at fleecing, the hotel makes guests pay a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pay a bomb' reads as British slang for a lot of money, but 'a bomb' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A depth charge is an explosive dropped to detonate underwater against submarines.

clue.text: Makes off, seeing current end-of-year measures?

parts.note: Dec is short for December, the month that ends the year
amps measure electric current, so current measures are amps

explanation.surface: Someone flees on noticing the new year's financial measures taking effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' and 'measures' together give AMPS, units of electric current, either side of the month abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to leave suddenly or secretly, which is making off.

clue.text: Visiting sister, went and arrived with a progress check

indicators.note: the visitors go into the home of the sister abbreviation, inside it

parts.note: peed is slang for went to the loo
came means arrived

explanation.surface: On a visit to a sister someone travelled, turned up, and checked on progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went' in its lavatorial sense gives PEED.
explanation.definitionFit: A speed camera checks how fast vehicles progress, catching speeding drivers.

clue.text: Unwelcome gift made undrinkable coffee, hated from the start by girl

parts.note: a drink that has been poisoned is no longer fit to drink

indicators.note: only the opening letter of each of the two words is taken

parts.note: Alice is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl hands over coffee she has spiked, having loathed the recipient all along.
explanation.definitionFit: A poisoned chalice is an idiom for an honour or job that looks attractive but brings harm.

clue.text: Hastened to adopt disguise for auditors

indicators.note: auditors are listeners, so the word is as heard rather than as written

parts.note: to hide is to conceal oneself, as a disguise does

explanation.surface: Someone rushed to put on a disguise before the accountants arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditors' looks like accountants but means listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: Hie is an old word for go quickly, so hied is the past tense meaning hurried.

clue.text: Toff in uniform was in the army secretly

indicators.note: the toff is dressed in the uniform, so the uniform's letter comes first

parts.note: U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a nob is a toff, an upper-class person
someone who was in the army served

explanation.surface: An upper-class man quietly did military service in uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something unobserved means doing it unseen, which is acting secretly.

clue.text: Manifest expectancy in stands ringing large field

indicators.note: the word for stands rings the other pieces, surrounding them

parts.note: to bear is to stand or tolerate
a lea is a field or meadow

explanation.surface: Spectators in the stands round a big field wait eagerly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stands' suggests spectator seating but means tolerates; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be all ears is an idiom for listening eagerly, showing keen anticipation.

clue.text: Rodent not lacking stomach eating a sort of light pastry

indicators.note: the rodent swallows the other letters, which go inside it

parts.note: a vole is a rodent
UV is ultraviolet light

indicators.note: a word's stomach is its middle letter, here removed

explanation.surface: A greedy rodent gobbles some flaky light pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light pastry' looks like the definition; 'light' belongs to UV.
explanation.definitionFit: A vol-au-vent is a small round case of puff pastry with a savoury filling.

clue.text: A thousand queuing to catch a fast train here?

definitions.text: to catch a fast train here?

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
people queuing are in line

explanation.surface: A thousand commuters queue for an express train.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'A' of 'A thousand' is used as it stands, after M.
explanation.definitionFit: A main line is a principal railway route where express trains run.

clue.text: Farmer being punched by small gang

indicators.note: the gang's letters punch a hole in the being and sit inside it

parts.note: a human is a being
a band is a gang

explanation.surface: A farmer is beaten up by a little gang.
explanation.definitionFit: Husbandman is an old word for a farmer, one who practises husbandry or tillage.

clue.text: Parasite's brief panic about pound

indicators.note: the shortened fear sits around the pound sign
a brief word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: fear is panic
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A sponger has a moment of alarm over a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' trims FEAR to FEA, which goes around L.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea is a blood-sucking insect living on a host, a classic parasite.

clue.text: Irrational to criticise thief

parts.note: pi is the best-known irrational number
to rate someone is an old use meaning to scold

explanation.surface: It is unreasonable to condemn a thief.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirate is a robber at sea, a kind of thief.

clue.text: Translating English literature, pens second half of proverb

indicators.note: translating changes the form of the words, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A translator renders English literature into another tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Translating' rearranges LITERATURE and PENS; E for English ends the answer. The proverb is 'Marry in haste, repent at leisure'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb's warning about hasty marriage closes with these three words, its second half.

clue.text: Mondrian's first to abrogate a religious genre

parts.note: the Dutch abstract painter Mondrian's first name supplies these letters

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Mondrian was the first to abolish a religious style of art.
explanation.definitionFit: A pietà is a type of artwork showing the Virgin Mary mourning the dead Christ.

clue.text: A little late, intentionally avoided any restaurant

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone, rather late and on purpose, skipped eating out.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat in is to dine at home rather than going out to a restaurant.

clue.text: Man alone before child

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: A man is left by himself before his child arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: An eremite is a hermit, a man who lives apart in solitude.

clue.text: A feeble prosecutor, so walk

parts.note: a lame excuse is a feeble one
DA is a district attorney, an American prosecutor

explanation.surface: A weak prosecutor gets a walkout.
explanation.definitionFit: An alameda is a public promenade, a tree-lined walk, in Spanish-speaking places.

clue.text: In safe space, nothing is to tease

indicators.note: nothing is put in the safe space, inside its letters

parts.note: a haven is a place of safety
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Somewhere safe, there is nothing to make fun of.
explanation.definitionFit: To have someone on is an idiom for kidding or teasing them.

clue.text: Summer weather coming in, button up dress

indicators.note: the summer weather comes in between the letters for hush

parts.note: sh is a call for silence; button up means keep quiet
heat is typical summer weather

explanation.surface: It is getting hot, so fasten your frock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'button up' looks like doing up clothes but means be quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath is a close-fitting, straight dress.
